Proteus Model Portfolio

Data as of --

Methodology

A model $100,000 book that holds up to six ETF positions — one per tracked market — chosen by a proprietary signal. Money is split equally across the positions held; when nothing qualifies, the book moves to cash, parked in short-term Treasury bills where it earns the prevailing money-market yield. The signal updates weekly, each Friday, and trades fill at the next session's close (normally Monday). Results include 5 basis points (bps) of trading cost per trade and assume no taxes; idle cash earns the 3-month Treasury-bill yield. This book holds the unleveraged ETFs.

Equity Curve

Current Holdings

Symbol% of PortfolioSharesFirst EnteredAverage Entry PriceCurrent PriceP&L %Max DD %MFE %Win

Holdings are the positions the book currently carries, one row per ETF. % of Portfolio is the position's share of the book; Shares is the number held; Average Entry Price is the cost-weighted average paid across any resizes while the position has been held; P&L % is the current price versus that average; Max DD % and MFE % are the worst drawdown and best gain of the position since it was first entered.

This Week's Actions

When the set of positions the book should hold changes, the whole book rebalances to an equal split: positions leaving are sold, then the remaining and new positions are each set to an equal share of the book. Sells are listed first, then buys, then the resize lines for positions that stay. If nothing changes, no trades are made and the weights are left to drift.

Every row is one completed position, from the session it was entered (Mon) to the session it was sold (Mon). Shares and % of Book are the size when it was opened. Return % is the exit price versus the entry price; P&L $ is the realized dollars on an average-cost basis, including any resizes while the position was held.
